goal: Every surface a person reads a plan on says what `origin/main` says, after a `git fetch`, and none of them reads a `PLAN.json` out of a workarea. Today `mc status <name>` prefers the workarea's copy (`src/mc/status-project.js` lines 258–272: `findWorkareaPlan` first, `origin/main` only when no workarea holds the file), and the page (`mc`) reads `origin/main` through `plans.json` without ever fetching unless `--fresh` is typed (`src/mc/page-collect.js` lines 1023–1045: the fetch is inside `if (fresh)`). A workarea's copy is whatever branch the folder happens to stand on, and the un-fetched `origin/main` is whatever the runner last fetched into `~/memoro` and `~/memoro-cli` — so with the runner idle, or a workarea left on an old branch, both surfaces show a plan that is not the one the runner will read. Martin, 2026-09-12: "Den ska göra git-anrop och läsa från main istället för lokala plan filer. Just nu ses inaktuell info." (ruling 20).

The page has a MERGES section: what is landing right now, what is queued for the runner's merge lane, and what is held before merge — the one story in order that today is split between a lock file nobody reads (`~/.memoro/mc/gate-running.json`, `src/mc/gate-lock.js`), two rows on NEXT's heading and the rows under its skips (`heldLines`, `queuedLines` in `src/mc/page-render.js` lines 586–645). The gate round that is running is not on the page at all: `gate-running.json` carries pid, repository slug, pull request and since (`takeGateLock`, `src/mc/gate-lock.js` line 70) and no surface reads it. Martin, 2026-09-12: "Låt oss visa 'merger'. Current + kö." (ruling 20).
contract: A plan is read from `origin/main` and from nowhere else on `mc`, `mc --json` and `mc status <name>`. The runner's own reading (`planOf` in `src/mc/run.js`, the worktree after `syncMain`) and the brief's are not touched by this project.

`git fetch -q origin` runs before the plans are read, on every print of the page and every live refresh, for every repository this machine has a checkout of, in parallel, through the same `exec` the page already fetches with under `--fresh`. `--offline` on the page and on `mc status` skips it and says so in the footer or the notes. `--fresh` keeps its meaning — fetch *and* ask GitHub for open pull requests — and the `prs.json` cache and its age line stay as they are.

The page's only writes stay the two read-through caches (`plans.json`, `prs.json`, `src/mc/page-cache.js`). The gate round gains one write of its own — its current phase into the lock file it already owns — and nothing else new is written anywhere.

`merges.json`, `held.json`, the gate lock and the repository lease keep their shapes and their writers; this project reads them. The one addition is two fields on `gate-running.json` (`phase`, `phase_at`) and one (`mode`), written only by the process whose pid the file names.

The page's order rule holds — what does not move sits above what does (`renderPageLines`, `src/mc/page-render.js` line 1057) — and no section that exists today is removed. `mc --json` stays one object with one key per section, and the front-door test's rule that every heading appears exactly once holds for the new heading too.
out_of_scope: Asking GitHub on every refresh. Open pull requests stay in `prs.json`, refilled by `--fresh` and by the runner's own readings; a stale open-PR list is a separate question with a `gh` call's cost behind it.
Any change to what the gate measures, how `mc merge` decides, how the merge lane orders its queue, or the one-repair rule. The section shows; it does not act.
A merge phase for `--docs` landings (`src/mc/docs-merge.js`): they take seconds, take no lock and leave no round to watch.
Removing the workarea reading from the runner's `machineState` (it asks a worktree whether it is dirty, not what its plan says) or from `mc brief`.
Writing the model, the lane or the runner's step into `gate-running.json`. The lock is the round's; what the runner is doing is RUNNER's.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc status <name>` reads the plan from `origin/main` after a fetch and never from a workarea, and the page fetches before every collect unless `--offline`.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/status-project.test.js`: a work root whose workarea checkout holds a newer `PLAN.json` than the injected `origin/main` prints main's steps and a `plan` row ending `(origin/main)`. `tests/mc/page.test.js` `collectPage`: the injected `exec` receives one `git … fetch -q origin` per present repository with `fresh: false`, and none with `offline: true`. Live: with a workarea deliberately left on an old branch (`git -C ~/mc/<name>/<repo> checkout <old-branch>`), `mc status <name>` prints the same STEPS rows as `git -C ~/memoro-cli show origin/main:docs/project/<programme>/<name>/PLAN.json` would.

success_criteria.criterion: A running gate round writes its phase into `gate-running.json`, and only the process that holds the lock can.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/gate-lock.test.js`: `noteGatePhase` on a file whose pid is this process rewrites `phase` and `phase_at` and keeps `pid`, `repo`, `pr`, `since`; on a file naming another pid it writes nothing and returns false. Live: during `mc test memoro-cli <pr>` (a `check` round), `cat ~/.memoro/mc/gate-running.json` shows a `phase` that changes as the round's stderr narration changes, and `mode: "check"`.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc` draws MERGES between NEXT and RUNNER with the landing round, the queue and the held pull requests, and `mc --json` carries `merges`.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/page.test.js` `the page`: the heading order is PROGRAMMES, INTAKE, WORK, NEXT, MERGES, RUNNER, HELPER, BRIEF; a fixture with a live lock draws `● memoro #11651` with its holder and phase; with a dead pid it draws `· nothing landing`; the queued and held rows are under MERGES and no longer under NEXT; `tests/mc/front-door.test.js` lists MERGES among the headings that appear exactly once. Live: while the runner is landing a pull request, `mc` shows that pull request under MERGES with the same phase `runner.log`'s `merge #N — …` line last said.

steps.title: Plans are read from origin/main after a fetch — on the page and in mc status
comments: findWorkareaPlan removed from src/mc/status-project.js; the plan row always reads (origin/main). collectPage fetches every present repository before loadPlans unless offline; mc --offline wires it through the live loop too. Footer distinguishes fetched/fresh/offline. Measured cost: ordinary fetch ~1.4-1.8s vs --offline ~0.4s on mc --json (2026-09-12); mc status <name> unaffected since it already fetched (1.7-2.3s live, 0.13-0.17s --offline). docs/technical/mc-status.md and mc-ui.md rewritten citing ruling 20. npm test: 1932 passed, 0 failed, 9 pre-existing skips.
steps.done_when: `collectProject` in `src/mc/status-project.js` no longer calls `findWorkareaPlan` and the function is gone; the `plan` row reads `(origin/main)`; `collectPage` in `src/mc/page-collect.js` fetches every present repository before `loadPlans` unless `offline`, and `mc --offline` sets it; the footer line says the page fetched; `docs/technical/mc-status.md` and `docs/technical/mc-ui.md` say so; the suite is green.
instruction: Read `collectProject` and `findWorkareaPlan` in `src/mc/status-project.js` (lines 186–201 and 242–335) and the tests that pin them in `tests/mc/status-project.test.js` (`finds it in the workarea checkout, under whichever programme` at line 140, `prefers the workarea plan, says it differs from main, and keeps the last three runs` at line 172, `falls back to origin/main when no workarea holds the plan` at line 188, and the render fixture at lines 325–340 that asserts `(workarea memoro-cli, differs from origin/main)`). Read `collectPage` in `src/mc/page-collect.js` (lines 1002–1127), `loadPlans` in `src/mc/page-cache.js`, the `--offline`/`--fresh` parsing in `src/mc/commands/home.js` (lines 117–125; `--offline` is accepted and does nothing today) and the footer line in `renderPageLines` (`src/mc/page-render.js` lines 1082–1090).

`mc status <name>`. Remove `findWorkareaPlan` and every use of it. The plan is `findMainPlan`'s and nothing else: `source` is always `'origin/main'`, so drop `source` and `unmerged` from the object `collectProject` returns and from `renderProject`, and let the `plan` row read `docs/project/<programme>/<name>/PLAN.json (origin/main)`. The workarea is still found (`existsSync(join(root, name))`) and still printed on the `workarea` row, and a name with a workarea and no plan on main still answers `no plan — this is a workarea without a project` — that case is unchanged. `machineState` keeps reading the workarea's worktree for dirtiness; that is a fact about the machine, not a plan. The fetch that already runs at the top of `collectProject` (line 253–256, skipped by `--offline`) is what makes `origin/main` current; keep it and keep its note on failure. `mc status --offline` should add a note saying the plan is `origin/main` as last fetched.

The page. In `collectPage`, take an `offline = false` option beside `fresh`, and fetch before `cache.loadPlans` whenever `!offline`: the same `exec('git', ['-C', repo.path, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin'])` per present repository, in one `Promise.all`, that the `fresh` branch runs today — lift it out of `if (fresh)` so both paths share one fetch and `fresh` only adds the `gh` calls. A failed fetch keeps the note it has (`<repo>: git fetch failed — plans may be stale`). `execAsync` in that file already has a 20 s timeout; a fetch that hangs must not hold the live loop past it, so keep that. Wire `--offline` in `src/mc/commands/home.js` to `collect({ fresh, offline })` in both places the page is collected (line 75 and 87); the live loop uses the same `collect` (`src/mc/page-live.js`), so a refresh fetches too, which is the point — read `page-live.js` to confirm the call goes through the same function and say in the PR body where.

The footer. `caches.fresh` drives the line `offline, PRs N old — --fresh asks GitHub`. Carry `caches.fetched: true|false` from `collectPage` (false under `--offline` or when every fetch failed) and draw: `fetched origin, PRs 3 min old — --fresh asks GitHub` for the ordinary page, `fresh — fetched and asked GitHub` for `--fresh` (unchanged), and `offline — plans as last fetched, PRs 3 min old` for `--offline`. `tests/mc/page.test.js` `the page` and `the palette` snapshot the footer; update the fixtures rather than loosening the assertions.

Measure once and write the number in the PR body: `time mc --json > /dev/null` three times with the fetch and three times with `--offline`, on this machine, so the cost of the fetch is on record beside the 1.1–1.8 s the page cost on 2026-09-03 (`docs/technical/mc-ui.md` § *What a refresh costs*).

Tests. `tests/mc/status-project.test.js`: replace the three tests named above with one that builds a work root whose workarea checkout holds a `PLAN.json` that differs from the injected `origin/main` text and asserts main's steps are printed and the `plan` row ends `(origin/main)`; keep the fallback test's other assertions (workarea path, runs). Delete the render fixture's `source`/`unmerged` and its `differs from` assertion. `tests/mc/page.test.js` `collectPage`: assert the injected `exec` is called with `fetch -q origin` for each present repository when `fresh` is false, and not at all when `offline` is true; the existing `--fresh` test keeps asserting the `gh` calls. `tests/mc/front-door.test.js` drives `mc --json | cat`; make sure its fixture's `exec` or environment does not now reach the network — inject `offline` or a stub `exec` there, and say which in the PR.

Docs. `docs/technical/mc-status.md`: rewrite § *The plan is read from the workarea, not from main* to say the opposite and why (the workarea copy is whatever branch the folder stands on; the runner reads main; Martin's words in ruling 20), and fix the table row *the plan, its state and its steps* and the example at the top that shows `(workarea memoro-cli)`. `docs/technical/mc-ui.md`: the surfaces table (`mc --fresh` row and add `mc --offline`), § *Where the facts come from* (plans are `origin/main` after a fetch), § *Why it is instant* and § *What a refresh costs* (a refresh now costs a fetch; give the number you measured), and the module comment at the top of `src/mc/page-collect.js` (`Offline is the default and the whole point` is no longer true). Cite ruling 20 by name. Run `npm test` once at the end, in the foreground.

In `gate-lock.js` add `noteGatePhase({ root = mcHome(), message, now = new Date() })`: read the file, return false unless it parses and `raw.pid === process.pid` (the same guard `releaseGateLock` uses, for the same reason — a reaped round's file may have been taken over), otherwise write it back through `writeJsonAtomic` with `phase: String(message).slice(0, 200)` and `phase_at: now.toISOString()` and every existing field kept, and return true. A write that throws returns false; the phase is a courtesy, like `onProgress`. Add `mode` to what `takeGateLock` writes, taken from a new `mode` option (default `null`), and pass it from `repo-gate.js` with the word the round log will use.

Call `noteGatePhase` from `say` in `repo-gate.js`, after `log` and before `onProgress`, so the file always says what the narration last said. It is one extra file write per narration line — count the lines a round emits (read `say(` calls in `repo-gate.js` and `repo-merge.js`) and say the number in the PR body; if it is more than a few dozen, throttle in `noteGatePhase` to one write per second by comparing `phase_at`, and say so.

The holder is the workarea name when the runner is landing (`landPr` in `src/mc/run.js` line 681 passes `{ name, kind: 'work-area' }`) and `user@host` when a person typed `mc merge`.

Tests in `tests/mc/gate-lock.test.js`: `noteGatePhase` on a file with this process's pid rewrites `phase` and `phase_at` and keeps the four existing fields; on a file with another (dead) pid writes nothing and returns false; on no file returns false. `takeGateLock` with `mode: 'check'` writes it. `runningMerge` with an injected `alive` maps a slug to its repository name and reads the lease beside it, and returns null for a dead pid.
